title: At the market
goal: Shop for fruit and vegetables at the market, and fit in adjectives: their place after the noun, and their forms that follow gender and number — plus the demonstrative "this".
bekal: ask for goods by quantity: *un kilogram de*, *o jumătate de kilogram de*, *o legătură de*
choose the adjective form that matches the noun: *bun, bună, buni, bune*
point at things with *acest pepene*, *pepenele acesta*, and the spoken form *ăsta / asta*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — La Piața Obor
dialogs.intro: On Saturday morning Budi goes shopping at Piața Obor, a big market in București. He stops at a fruit and vegetable stall.

lines.speaker: Vânzătoarea:
lines.id: Good morning! Go ahead, what would you like?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Good morning. Are the tomatoes fresh?

lines.speaker: Vânzătoarea:
lines.text: Sigur, sunt foarte proaspete, de azi-dimineață.
lines.id: Of course, they're very fresh, from this morning.
lines.literal: sure, they-are very fresh-f-pl, from today-morning.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Bine. Un kilogram de roșii, vă rog.
lines.id: Good. A kilo of tomatoes, please.
lines.literal: good. a-m kilogram of tomatoes, you-pl I-ask.

lines.speaker: Vânzătoarea:
lines.text: Poftiți. Avem și mere. Merele acestea sunt foarte dulci.
lines.id: Here you are. We have apples too. These apples are very sweet.
lines.literal: please-pl. we-have also apples. apples-the these-f they-are very sweet-pl.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Atunci o jumătate de kilogram de mere. Și cât costă pepenii?
lines.id: Then half a kilo of apples. And how much are the watermelons?
lines.literal: then a-f half of kilogram of apples. and how-much they-cost watermelons-the?

lines.speaker: Vânzătoarea:
lines.text: Trei lei kilogramul. Pepenii sunt mari și dulci.
lines.id: Three lei a kilo. The watermelons are big and sweet.
lines.literal: three lei kilogram-the. watermelons-the they-are big-pl and sweet-pl.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Acest pepene este prea mare. Aveți și pepeni mici?
lines.id: This watermelon is too big. Do you have small ones too?

lines.text: Da, ăsta este mic și bun. Are patru kilograme.
lines.id: Yes, this one is small and good. It weighs four kilos.

lines.text: Perfect. Și o legătură de pătrunjel, vă rog.

notes: **Un kilogram de roșii — quantities always link with *de*.** The pattern is the same as *douăzeci de lei* in unit 5: quantity + *de* + noun **without the article**, just like English "a kilo of". Countable things go in the plural (*de roșii, de mere*), uncountable things stay singular (*de pătrunjel, de brânză*).
**Roșiile = "the tomatoes".** The chain: *roșie* (one tomato) → *roșii* (plural) → *roșiile* (plural with the definite article, the *-le* ending from unit 6).

**Proaspete follows *roșiile*.** This is the point of this unit: a Romanian adjective always copies the gender and number of its noun — even when *sunt* stands between them. *Roșiile* is feminine plural, so *proaspete*; *pepenii* is masculine plural, so *mari și dulci*.

**Acest pepene, merele acestea, ăsta.** Three faces of "this" in one dialogue: the short form in front of a bare noun, the form with *-a* after a noun with the article, and the spoken form *ăsta / asta* in the mouths of market traders.

**Poftiți and Atât.** *Poftiți* is a seller's all-purpose word: "go ahead", "here are your things", "here's your change". *Atât* literally means "that much" — the standard answer to *Mai doriți ceva?*.

grammars.title: Adjectives — behind the noun, and matching it
body: First, the position: unlike English, Romanian adjectives come **after** the noun. *O roșie proaspătă* = "a tomato fresh", *un pepene mare* = "a watermelon big".
What's new: the adjective changes its ending to match the gender and number of the noun. There are at most four forms, and many adjectives have only three or two.
after: **The basic pattern: — , -ă, -i, -e**, exactly the noun endings you already know. The sound changes are the same as in unit 5: *-i* softens the consonant (*frumos → frumoși*, *proaspăt → proaspeți*), and *o* becomes *oa* in the feminine (*frumos → frumoasă*).
**Adjectives ending in *-e*** (*mare, dulce, verde*) don't distinguish gender — only singular versus plural. Adjectives ending in *-c* or *-esc* have one plural form for both: *mici*, *românești*.
**Neuter nouns** stay true to their nature: masculine form in the singular, feminine form in the plural. *Un măr bun* → *două mere bune*; *un bilet scump* → *bilete scumpe*.
**After *a fi* the rule is the same:** *Cafeaua este bună. Pepenii sunt mari. Merele sunt dulci.* But *foarte* (very) and *prea* (too) never change: *foarte bună, prea mari*.

grammars.title: Demonstratives — acest pepene, pepenele acesta, pepenele ăsta
body: Romanian has two ways to say "this watermelon", and they mean exactly the same. The only difference is where the demonstrative stands — and that decides whether the noun takes the article.
after: **Don't mix them.** In front: short form + bare noun (*acest pepene*). Behind: noun with article + form with *-a* (*pepenele acesta*). *Acest pepenele* and *pepene acesta* are both wrong. The front order is neater and common in writing; the back order, especially with *ăsta / asta*, is everyday speech.
**Neuter nouns** split again: *acest măr* → *aceste mere*; *mărul acesta* → *merele acestea*.

**Standing alone**, use the form with *-a*: *Acesta este mic* ("This one is small"), *Aceasta este Ioana*. *Asta* also means "this / that" in general, without pointing to a particular noun: *Ce este asta?* (What's this?), *Cât costă asta?* (How much is this?), *Asta e tot* (That's all).

blocks.title: At a Romanian market
items: **Pepene** on its own can mean two fruits. To be clear: *pepene roșu* ("red melon") = watermelon, *pepene galben* ("yellow melon") = melon. Watermelons from Dăbuleni, in the south of the country, are what sellers boast about most.
**Piața Obor** is one of the biggest and oldest markets in București. Grilled *mici* at Obor — skinless minced-meat sausages, eaten with mustard and bread — are a destination in themselves.
Prices are written per kilogram. Some things are sold *la bucată* (per piece), and leafy greens like *pătrunjel* (parsley) or *ceapă verde* (spring onions) are sold per *legătură* — per bunch.

sections.title: Quantities and phrases at the stall

blocks.text: *Kilogram* is neuter, so in the plural the number takes the feminine form: *două kilograme*, not *doi*. At the stall you'll also hear the short form, *un kil*. And remember: after *de* the noun is always bare — *un kilogram de roșii*, never *de roșiile*.

blocks.title: Two things about money at the market
items: **Bring cash.** Many stalls only accept *numerar* (cash), and sellers are happy if you have small notes. A question you'll hear often: *Aveți mărunt?* — "Do you have small change?"
**Haggling isn't really the custom.** Prices are usually written on a small sign and apply as they are.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right form of the adjective.
Move the demonstrative behind the noun (example: acest pepene → pepenele acesta).
